# Psalm 141 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A psalm of David. LORD, I'm calling out to you — hurry! Listen to my voice when I cry out to you!

**2** Let my prayer rise before you like incense; let my lifted hands be like an evening offering.

**3** LORD, put a guard at my mouth! Watch over the door of my lips!

**4** Don't let my heart be drawn toward evil or let me join in wicked activities with people who do wrong — and don't let me enjoy their luxuries.

**5** Let a good person correct me — that's an act of kindness. Let them rebuke me — that's like healing oil on my head. I won't refuse it. But I will keep praying against the wicked.

**6** When their leaders are thrown down from the cliff, people will realize my words were true.

**7** Our bones are scattered at the edge of the grave, like dirt turned up by a plow.

**8** But my eyes are fixed on you, LORD my God. I take shelter in you — don't let me die!

**9** Protect me from the traps they've set for me and from the snares of evildoers.

**10** Let the wicked get caught in their own nets — while I walk safely past.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **141:3**: 'Put a guard at my mouth' — this prayer is so honest. We all know we can't control our own words. The psalmist doesn't say 'I'll try harder'; he says 'God, you need to stand guard.'

— PNEUMA
